PE1-23.hint: A change inside the parentheses acts on \(x\) and moves the graph sideways, opposite to how the sign looks. A change outside acts on the output.
slips: Shifting right for \(x + 3\). Inside changes work backward: \(x + 3\) moves the graph left.
Shifting up because of the minus sign in front of \(f\). The \(-5\) outside shifts down; the leading minus reflects.
Putting the stretch factor inside the parentheses: \((2x+3)^{2}\) is not the same as \(2(x+3)^{2}\).
PE1-23.source: Practice Exam 1 review (the 38 questions on the Exam 1 review site, 172exam1review)

PE1-24.hint: Move the vertex first: how far right or left, how far up or down. "Opens downward" means a reflection across the \(x\)-axis. "Same width" means no stretch or compression.
slips: Writing \(f(x+2)\) for a shift right \(2\). To move right, subtract inside.
Writing \(+3\) at the end. The vertex moved down, so subtract.
Leaving out the reflection, which gives a graph that opens upward.
PE1-24.source: Practice Exam 1 review (the 38 questions on the Exam 1 review site, 172exam1review)

PE1-33.hint: Compare key points. Where is the vertex or starting point of \(g\) compared with \(f\)? Does \(g\) open the same way as \(f\)? Is it steeper or flatter?
slips: Writing \(|x+1|\) for a shift right \(1\). To move right, subtract inside.
Missing the vertical stretch. In panel A, \(g\) changes by \(2\) units for each \(1\) unit sideways, where \(f\) changes by \(1\).
Missing the reflection in panel A. The graph of \(g\) opens downward.
PE1-33.source: Practice Exam 1 review (the 38 questions on the Exam 1 review site, 172exam1review)

PE1-37.hint: Track the starting point of the square root. Then notice which way the graph opens: a graph that opens to the left has been reflected across the \(y\)-axis.
slips: Writing \(f(-x+2)\). That shifts the graph right \(2\), because \(-x + 2 = -(x - 2)\).
Reflecting across the \(x\)-axis. That would send the graph downward, not to the left.
Forgetting the domain. The radicand \(-x-2\) must be at least \(0\), so \(x \le -2\).
PE1-37.source: Practice Exam 1 review (the 38 questions on the Exam 1 review site, 172exam1review)

parts.q: Describe the sequence of transformations that produces \(g(x) = -f(x+3) - 5\) from the parent function \(f(x)\).
parts.a: Shift left \(3\), reflect across the \(x\)-axis, then shift down \(5\).

parts.q: Let \(f(x) = x^{2}\). Write \(g(x)\) if the graph of \(f\) is shifted left \(3\) units, vertically stretched by a factor of \(2\), and shifted up \(4\) units.

items.stem: The parent function \(f(x) = |x|\) has its vertex at \((0,0)\). A transformed function \(g(x)\) has its vertex at \((2,-3)\), opens downward, and has the same width as the parent function.

parts.q: Write the coordinate mapping for the vertex.

items.stem: Each panel shows a parent function \(f\) (dashed) and its transformed graph \(g\) (solid). In panel A, \(f(x) = |x|\). In panel B, \(f(x) = \sqrt{x}\). For each panel, describe the transformations from \(f\) to \(g\), then write an equation for \(g\).

parts.a: Shift right \(1\), stretch vertically by a factor of \(2\), reflect across the \(x\)-axis, and shift up \(3\): \(g(x) = -2|x-1| + 3\).

figures.alt: Two graphs side by side on coordinate grids, labeled A and B. Both show a dashed graph of f and a solid graph of g, each labeled with its letter. Panel A: the dashed graph is a V shape with its corner at (0, 0). The solid graph is an upside-down V with its peak at (1, 3); it passes through the marked points (0, 1) and (2, 1) and falls steeply on both sides. Panel B: the dashed graph is a square root curve that starts at (0, 0) and rises to the right. The solid graph is a curve of the same shape that starts at the marked point (-2, -1) and passes through the marked points (-1, 0) and (2, 1). Both panels show x and y from about -3 to 5. A table of the marked points on g is below the graphs.

items.stem: The graph shows the parent function \(f(x) = \sqrt{x}\) (dashed) and a transformed graph \(g\) (solid).

parts.a: Reflect \(f\) across the \(y\)-axis, then shift it left \(2\) units. The starting point moves from \((0,0)\) to \((-2,0)\).

parts.q: Write \(g(x)\) in terms of \(f\), and then as an explicit formula.
